args.body: IMPOSSIBLE, by a theorem and not by a simulation: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency. This is the strongest verdict anything in this repository can return short of Lean: not "unlikely", not "inefficient", but zero net displacement per cycle, at any beat frequency, for any organism whose stroke retraces its own path at this Reynolds number. Driving the power stroke faster than the recovery stroke -- the obvious fix, and the one intuition suggests -- changes nothing, because in the Stokes limit the displacement depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate.

detail.theorem: Purcell EM 1977, Life at low Reynolds number, Am J Phys 45(1):3-11
detail.limiting_factor: the stroke is time-reversible (declared reciprocal) and Re <= 9.96e-5 everywhere in the stated ranges. In the Stokes limit the displacement over a cycle depends on the PATH through configuration space and not on the rate, so a path that retraces itself returns the body exactly where it started. Net displacement per cycle is zero, at any beat frequency.
detail.what_would_fix_it: break the time-reversal symmetry: a rotating helix, a travelling wave along a flagellum, or a cilium whose recovery stroke follows a different path from its power stroke. Two or more degrees of freedom moved out of phase trace a loop, and a loop encloses area, and enclosed area is displacement.

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
